entry.title: 导航与历史：Panel ↔ 路由、返回与无焦点跟随

content.markdown:
## 语义目的地

共享阅读层输出导航意图：Library 列表、Library slug、独立 Entry（含 Package）、Library occurrence（slug + node ID + Entry）、相关 Entry 和返回目的地。结构化上下文不能简化为 Entry ID、按钮文字或偶然 DOM 位置。引用目标不在当前 Library 时允许独立 Entry；重复 occurrence 必须保留身份。源码显式快捷键先按稳定 Entry 全序选定 Entry，再在可用 occurrence 中按 node ID 的 UTF-16 码元字典序选择最小项；无 occurrence 才用独立 Entry。不能依赖偶然 DOM 顺序。普通阅读导航仍保留明确指定 occurrence。

Extension adapter 打开/复用正确 Panel，并保存源码 editor group 与返回上下文。HTML adapter 编码 URL/hash，支持直接深链接、刷新、前进/后退和明确返回。Entry 标题、关系和弹窗导航复用同一 router；不得另建一个源码专用简化 Entry 页面。

## 显式导航和被动跟随

点击/快捷键是显式导航，可增加一条有意义历史并聚焦目标。被动源码跟随只更新对应文档目的地/高亮，保持 Monaco/IDE 焦点，不为每次 caret 移动追加历史。区分 push、replace/同步和返回恢复，不把程序 selection 或滚动再次反馈成新用户导航。保存 origin/request token 或等价防回声语义。

后退恢复 Library/occurrence、相关返回上下文及允许保存的阅读/源码位置；普通刷新重读同一语义目的地，不偷偷返回列表。没有合法返回目的地时给出明确首页入口，不伪装历史栈。损坏/未知/快照不含的路由要可解释地报不可用，不猜测或跳到另一 Entry。

## 能力边界与验收

编辑、系统外 URL、源码定位是不同意图，分别授权；无源码导出不能通过通用路由泄露本机路径。可编码目的地不等于已支持 multi-root：继承 source-document 的 root 歧义拒绝规则。

对比 Library A 的第二 occurrence → related Entry → 子弹窗 Entry → 返回 → 源码反查 → 后退/前进；再从复制 URL 直接打开并刷新。检查身份、选区、焦点、历史长度和失效目标，不能用 mock 消息发送证明浏览器历史已工作。

## BrowserReader 的 SNoogL 与图谱入口

交互式 HTML 在现有阅读器中接入 SNoogL 和关系图路由，沿用同一共享 UI、浏览器历史和 Entry 阅读出口。SNoogL 复用 SnooglApp 与现有搜索/跨域筛选语义，支持 Entry/Macro 切换、查询、Kind 与关联对象过滤、键盘选择和结果阅读。明确显示搜索范围是本次导出快照，不能将局部闭包标称全工作区；不为搜索私自扩大导出闭包。Entry 结果进入共享 Entry 路由；Macro 结果有实际只读预览及已导出的来源 Entry 导航，不能跳到不可用的宏编辑器或显示空按钮。搜索与图入口提供返回阅读上下文，Entry 返回可回到来源搜索/图；URL 可直接打开、刷新、前进和后退。现有 Library occurrence 与源码跟随路由继续有效。

源码—文档双向定位直接复用 sourceExport/viewer 的只读 Monaco、正向范围、反向范围选择、Ctrl+Alt+J 与无焦点/无新增历史的被动跟随，不另造同步机制。此阅读能力不等于编辑源码或持久写回仓库，后者不在本次接入范围。

SNoogL 同类路由的显式导航、刷新和浏览器历史必须同步恢复查询、模式和筛选；本地键入不重建输入框、不逐字符增加历史。


## Local Web host compatibility

The Toolkit local Web host and HTML exports share ReaderRoute identity, codec and browser navigation rather than fork routing implementations. Local routes add explicit Library context; existing standalone export routes retain their meaning. Local HTTP loading and frozen snapshot/resource handling are distinct adapters. The local shell reuses BrowserReader, SNoogL and the graph and marks itself as current-workspace read-only, not a frozen export. Context changes reject stale async replies. Local-only workspace navigation must not leak into static export behavior. Future edit destinations use this same routing system with host capabilities; static exports never gain a write adapter.


## Unified local reader header

The local Web host must use the Extension's shared PanelHeader, native controls, branding, typography, spacing, preferences and language selectors, not a copied header or stacked shell/navigation bars. Each active workspace, Library, Entry, Macro, search and graph route has one visible top-level header. Desktop controls occupy one row; narrow layouts preserve access to all controls without page-level horizontal overflow. Integrate Refresh, workspace/back navigation, SNoogL and graph navigation and a compact read-only indication into the shared header. Do not duplicate Back or graph entry points. Preserve context-specific title and navigation behavior, including Library occurrence identity and browser history. Loading, empty and failure states retain usable header navigation and refresh. Shared component defaults in the Extension and frozen HTML remain compatible; local-only host actions must not leak into static HTML or authoring contexts.

The local service follows workspace file changes automatically using a host-owned change notification stream. Notifications invalidate the current catalog and selected Library snapshot; manual Refresh remains available. Static HTML remains frozen and requires regeneration; neither automatic following nor the shared header adds editing or source-view support.


## Shared workspace Library list

The local Web workspace page and Extension Dashboard must import the same Library table component rather than maintaining a plain link list or a visual copy. Preserve the Dashboard table typography, spacing, title/slug columns, numeric statistics, row hover/focus and keyboard activation. The read-only host supplies reading navigation instead of edit intents and omits all create/delete controls and their empty action column. Keep the single PanelHeader; loading, empty and failure states remain usable. Long titles/slugs and narrow screens must not overflow the page: retain accessible table content with a local scroll region or wrapping as appropriate. Shared component defaults preserve Dashboard authoring behavior and interface localization.

The workspace API supplies Library statistics from already-read Library graphs, without fetching/rendering each Library snapshot. Match current Dashboard semantics: entryCount counts distinct Entry-labelled graph node IDs (occurrences, not distinct shared Entry IDs); relationshipCount counts Library graph edges, not global semantic relationships. Unknown/omitted counts display an em dash, not zero. Refresh rereads these derived values; they are not authoring state or a new persistent index. These statistics add no editing or source-view capability.


## Automatic local file following

The local service owns one workspace-scoped filesystem watcher, shared by browser subscribers. Observe authored `.SNL_Doc` configuration, entities, Libraries and assets, including additions, deletion, atomic replacement and newly created directories. Do not traverse symlinks or observe derived cache/lock/temporary churn as authored updates. Coalesce save bursts into bounded notifications. Directory replacement and watcher failures must not silently disable updates: expose an unavailable state and retry/recover. No whole-snapshot polling or per-tab filesystem watcher is required.

`GET /__snl/api/events` is a same-origin read-only SSE endpoint behind the existing Host/Origin/method checks. Emit an initial `change` event with an opaque `revision` on each connection and a new revision after changes; event payloads contain no file paths or content. `unavailable` reports a safe watcher-status message. HEAD completes without subscribing. Heartbeats, slow-client handling and cleanup bound the resources; client disconnect, server close and failed startup release streams, timers and watches.

The local reader subscribes once, closes its EventSource and timers on unmount, ignores late callbacks, coalesces notifications and deduplicates revisions within a healthy connection. Initial/recovered connections force a current read even for an unchanged revision so reconnect catches missed edits. Preserve current Library/Entry/node/search/graph hash and browser history; updates must not navigate home or push new history entries. Retain usable previous content while replacement reads are pending, label read/connection failures visibly and recover on the next accepted update. Bind every success/error to the active Library and generation. Manual refresh remains usable while following is disconnected. Preserve ordinary reading position where feasible; arbitrary transient graph camera/disclosure state is not a guaranteed persistent state across rebuilt snapshots. This feature applies only to the live local Web host, not frozen HTML or file writeback.
